title: FX-C4: DtoProjection.ToPropertyDto skips structural redaction — SecureString leak
description:
## Finding (Opus review: security)

**File:** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/Infrastructure/DtoProjection.cs:66-69`

`ToPropertyDto` calls `RedactionFilter.IsRedacted(name, propertyType)` (name + declared-type match) but does **not** call `RedactionFilter.IsStructurallySensitive(prop.Value)`. The latter catches runtime `SecureString`, `NetworkCredential`, `DbConnectionStringBuilder`, and `[Sensitive]`-typed objects.

Consequence: a property with an innocuous name (e.g. `DataContext`, `Tag`, `ViewModel`) whose runtime value is a `NetworkCredential` serialises the `ToString()` into the MCP response without redaction.

## Fix

In `ToPropertyDto`, before computing `isRedacted`, call `RedactionFilter.IsStructurallySensitive(prop.Value)` and short-circuit to `StringValue = "[REDACTED]"` + `IsRedacted = true` regardless of `enableRedaction`.

## Acceptance

- Test: property named `Tag` holding a `NetworkCredential` → DTO StringValue == `[REDACTED]`.
- Test: property named `Data` holding a `[Sensitive]`-typed value → redacted.
- Build + full test suite clean.

## Scope

- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/Infrastructure/DtoProjection.cs`
- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Tests/Infrastructure/DtoProjectionStructuralRedactionTests.cs` (new)

## M2-21: `SnoopWPF.Agent.BrokerHost` broker scaffolding (new library)

> **NEW 2026-04-16** per architecture change. Read
> `ARCHITECTURE-CHANGE-2026-04-16-BROKERED-MODE.md` first.

**PRD ref:** PRD §4.1 Brokered mode. Generic broker pieces only —
lifecycle tools like `mc_launch` are MC-specific and live in the MC
repo's `UiMcpHost` project, not here.
**Depends on:** M1-21 (`StartBrokered`), M1-22 (pipe framing).
**Estimated:** ~500 LOC + tests.

**Scope**

Create a **new project** `SnoopWPF.Agent.BrokerHost/` (type ClassLibrary,
`net8.0-windows`). The existing `SnoopWPF.Agent.Host` is the injection-mode
`snoop-mcp.exe` (OutputType=Exe, `AssemblyName=snoop-mcp`) and stays
completely unchanged. Do NOT modify it.

`SnoopWPF.Agent.BrokerHost` exposes:

- `BrokerHost.Start(McpServerTransport transport, BrokerOptions opts)` —
  sets `Console.SetOut(TextWriter.Null)` as its first statement (broker owns
  MCP stdio), then installs the 18-tool MCP surface; each tool routes through
  a pipe client to whichever target is currently connected.
- `BrokerOptions.PipeName` — name of the pipe to connect to.
- `BrokerOptions.OnTargetDisconnected` — callback hook for external lifecycle
  code (MC's `UiMcpHost` uses this to surface `TARGET_NOT_RUNNING` failures).
- Generic tool-proxy registration that downstream consumers extend with their
  own lifecycle tools (`mc_launch`, etc).
- `BrokerTargetSpawner.Spawn(exe, args, pipeName, tokenHex)` — calls
  `Process.Start` with `UseShellExecute=false`, `CreateNoWindow=true`,
  `RedirectStandardOutput=true`, `RedirectStandardError=true`. Spawns
  background drain-tasks that read and discard target stdout/stderr (optionally
  forward to a log file, never to broker's stdout).
- No MC-specific code in this project — lifecycle tools belong to the external
  broker consuming this library.

**Files to create** (all under `SnoopWPF.Agent.BrokerHost/`)

  `StartInfo.RedirectStandardOutput == true`.
- Integration test: broker launches sample target with
  `--snoop-pipe=<name> --snoop-token=<hex>`; target's stdout does NOT appear
  on broker's stdout (assert by reading broker's stdio for 500 ms, confirm
  empty).

title: FX-C3: Handshake transmits plaintext session token (server teaches secret)
description:
## Finding (Opus review: security)

**File:** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Server/McpServerSetup.cs:151-154`, `SnoopWPF.Agent.Contracts/Protocol/HandshakeChallenge.cs:12`

The server-speaks-first handshake sends the raw session token to whoever connects, then verifies that the client echoes it back verbatim:

\`\`\`csharp
var challenge = new HandshakeChallenge
{
    SessionToken = sessionToken,   // ← token sent in clear
    ProtocolVersion = ProtocolConstants.ProtocolVersion,
};
await SendFramedJsonAsync(pipeStream, challenge, ct);
\`\`\`

Any same-user process that wins the connect race learns the token. `PipeOptions.CurrentUserOnly` prevents cross-user attacks only.

## Fix

Redesign handshake:

1. Server generates a random 16-byte nonce per connection attempt.
2. Server sends `HandshakeChallenge { Nonce, ProtocolVersion }` (no token).
3. Client returns `HandshakeResponse { ProofHmac = HMACSHA256(nonce, sessionToken), ProtocolVersion }`.
4. Server computes expected HMAC with its copy of the token, `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`.

Token never traverses the pipe.

## Acceptance

- Protocol version bump (ProtocolConstants.ProtocolVersion +1).
- Both sides rewritten consistently (BrokerHost target-side + Remote proxy client-side).
- Handshake integration test verifying a wrong-token connect is rejected.

## Scope

- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Contracts/Protocol/HandshakeChallenge.cs`
- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Contracts/Protocol/HandshakeResponse.cs` (new)
- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Server/McpServerSetup.cs` (PerformPipeHandshakeAsync)
- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Remote/PipeSnoopInspectorProxy.cs` (client side)
- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Tests/HandshakeSecurityTests.cs` (new)

title: FX-N1: Wire AuditLogWriter to production paths
description:
## Finding (Opus review: security)

`AuditLogWriter` (HMAC-chained audit log) is fully implemented and unit-tested but never instantiated in production. `SnoopAgent`, `McpServerSetup`, and `BrokerHost` do not wire it up. Audit entries are never written at runtime — HMAC chain is a dead-letter guarantee.

## Fix

1. In `SnoopAgent.StartCoLocated` + `StartBrokered` + `BrokerHost.RunAsync`: instantiate `AuditLogWriter` if `SnoopAgentOptions.AuditLogPath` is set.
2. In each tool handler (via a shared `Tool.InvokeAsync` wrapper or explicit call): emit `AuditEntry { Tool, Args, Policy, Result, Timestamp }` on both success and failure.
3. Dispose writer on agent handle disposal.
4. Integration test: tool invocation → audit file has valid HMAC chain.

## Acceptance

- `SnoopAgentOptions.AuditLogPath` gated opt-in.
- Each tool invocation produces one audit entry.
- HMAC chain verifies end-to-end.
- Build + tests clean.

## Scope

- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Server/SnoopAgent.cs`
- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Server/McpServerSetup.cs`
- `SnoopWPF.Agent.BrokerHost/BrokerHost.cs`
- `SnoopWPF.Agent.IntegrationTests/AuditLogIntegrationTests.cs` (new)

title: FX-M8: MaxTier not enforced in SnoopInspector mutation methods
description:
## Finding

**File:** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/SnoopInspector.cs` (all mutation methods)

`SessionPolicy.MaxTier` is set to `L0ReadOnly` for Injection mode but `SnoopInspector` never reads `policy.MaxTier` — each method only checks `this.options.EnableMutation`. `MaxTier` is enforced only in `InputStrategySelector` (separate assembly, not wired into the engine).

Caller setting `EnableMutation=true, MaxTier=L0ReadOnly` on a Brokered session can still invoke all mutations.

## Fix

Add `EnsureMutationTier(policy)` helper at top of each mutation method (`SetPropertyAsync`, `SetCheckStateAsync`, `SetTextValueAsync`, `SetSliderValueAsync`, `SelectItemAsync`, `ClickAsync`, `ToggleAsync`, `ExpandCollapseAsync`, `ExecuteCommandAsync`). Return `StateDeltaDto { Success=false, FailureReason=TierExceeded }` if `policy.MaxTier < InputTier.L1`.

## Acceptance

- Test: `MaxTier=L0ReadOnly + EnableMutation=true` → all 9 mutation methods return TierExceeded.
- `SessionPolicyTests` still passes.
- Build + tests clean.

## Scope

- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/SnoopInspector.cs`
- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Tests/SnoopInspectorTierEnforcementTests.cs` (new)

title: FX-C2: SnoopAgentHandle.Dispose is not thread-safe
description:
## Finding

**File:** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Server/SnoopAgentHandle.cs:59-71`

- Build + tests clean.

description:
## Finding

PRD §7.6 spec: `{ success: true, stateChanged: false, treeVersionDelta: 0, failureReason: STATE_UNCHANGED, suggestion: wpf_inspect_element }`.

- `StateChangedSerializationTests` covers all 5.

title: FX6-A1: wpf_wait_for_property — unbounded timeoutMs → semaphore starvation DoS
description:
## Finding (R7-A, CRITICAL)

**File:** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Tools/WaitForPropertyTool.cs:~58` + `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/SnoopInspector.cs::WaitForPropertyAsync`

`timeoutMs` parameter is clamped to `[0, int.MaxValue]` with no upper bound. A prompt-injected request with `timeoutMs=86400000` (24h) holds the inspector's concurrency semaphore for the full duration, starving all other tool calls.

## Fix

Clamp `timeoutMs` to a configurable ceiling (default 30000ms) via `SnoopAgentOptions.MaxWaitForPropertyMs`. Emit `FailureReason.InvalidArgument` with `suggestion={reduceTimeout}` when exceeded.

## Acceptance

- `WaitForPropertyToolTests.TimeoutClampedToCeiling` passes
- `SnoopAgentOptionsTests.MaxWaitForPropertyMs_DefaultMatchesPrd` passes
- No semaphore starvation under concurrent 30s polls

Cursor tokens store `(offset, pageSize, totalCount)` but are NOT bound to the `nodeId` or `snapshotEpoch` they were issued from. A cursor issued from tool `wpf_get_children(nodeId=A)` can be replayed against `wpf_get_children(nodeId=B)` and return B's data with A's offset — cross-node data leak visible to the agent.

## Fix

Include `nodeId + epoch` in the cursor payload (HMAC-signed with session secret). Reject mismatched nodeId with `SnoopException(CursorMismatch)`.

title: FX6-A3: WaitForPropertyAsync — NodeRegistry unbounded OOM
description:
## Finding (R7-A, HIGH)

**File:** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/SnoopInspector.cs::WaitForPropertyAsync`

Every poll iteration calls `NodeRegistry.Resolve(nodeId)` which re-walks the tree and caches a new entry. Over a 30s poll at 100ms interval this is 300 registry entries per call; under concurrent waits the registry grows without bound.

title: FX6-A4: SnoopInspector — ODE/IOE/AggregateException escape tool-layer catches
description:
## Finding (R7-A / R7-H, HIGH)

**Files:** SnoopWPF.Agent.Tools/*.cs (all 28 tool handlers)

Tools catch `SnoopException` and `OperationCanceledException` but let `ObjectDisposedException` / `InvalidOperationException` / `AggregateException` escape as raw class names to the MCP client. LLM sees e.g. "ObjectDisposedException: Cannot access a disposed object" which breaks its error-recovery heuristics.

## Fix

Add a shared `ToolExceptionMapper.Wrap(Func<Task<string>>)` that maps:
- ODE → `SnoopException(AgentDisposed)`
- IOE → `SnoopException(InvalidState)`
- AE → unwrap first inner, recurse

## Acceptance

Move DP enumeration off Dispatcher (snapshot via `DependencyObject.GetLocalValueEnumerator` inline, then marshal only the page window back to Dispatcher for value resolution).

## Finding (R7-C, CRITICAL)

**File:** `SnoopWPF.Agent/SnoopAgent.cs::StartAsync` (approx line 80-120)

StartAsync wraps server startup in `Task.Run(() => StartServerAsync(...))` without await. If startup throws (invalid options, port bound, etc.), the exception is swallowed into the unobserved Task. `Trace.TraceError` is invisible in stdio MCP mode (no trace listener configured).

Result: agent appears to start successfully, MCP client connects, first tool call hangs forever.

## Fix

- Await the startup task synchronously OR
- Route exceptions to an `IStartupFailureSink` that writes to the configured AuditLog AND writes a single framed MCP error to stderr
- Expose `StartAsync` that returns `Task<SnoopAgentHandle>` where Handle has an `IsStarted` property + `StartupException`

## Fix

- Fail-fast at StartAsync: attempt a 0-byte write to the audit path; on failure throw `SnoopException(AuditUnwritable)` with the target path + inner exception

title: Replace RenderTargetBitmap with Windows.Graphics.Capture for wpf_capture_screenshot
description:
## Problem

`wpf_capture_screenshot` is broken on any non-trivial window and violates the brokered-MCP feature's \"fast & reliable\" goal (DESKTOP-11470).

**Observed against live MotionCatalyst (MC-1a Phase 3 validation, 2026-04-17):**

- Full-window capture of MC main window (1382×879, `SwingCatalystMainGui`) fails **100%** of the time with `DISPATCHER_BUSY`
- Small sub-region capture (caption bar 1378×26) succeeds **instantly**
- Subsequent screenshot calls are poisoned by orphaned ops — self-starving loop

## Root cause

`ScreenshotCapture.CaptureAsPng` uses `RenderTargetBitmap` via `VisualCaptureUtil.RenderVisualWithHighQuality`. RTB runs the full WPF render pipeline **synchronously on the UI dispatcher**.

For a complex window with chrome + D3D interop:

1. Render work takes ≥500ms just to start → `SnoopInspector.DispatcherAcceptanceTimeoutMs` (500) fires
2. `dispatcherOp.Abort()` **does not cancel** a started `InvokeAsync` — WPF has no cancellable InvokeAsync contract
3. The orphaned render op keeps running on the dispatcher, starves subsequent `DispatcherPriority.Send` work
4. D3D-interop content (MC's video preview surfaces) renders **black** in RTB regardless — separate known issue

RTB is fundamentally the wrong API for this use case.

## Fix: Windows.Graphics.Capture (WGC)

Replace RTB with `Windows.Graphics.Capture` (WinRT, Windows 10 1903+):

- Runs **off the UI thread** — only needs the HWND
- **GPU-side composited frame** — captures exactly what DWM shows, including D3D-interop content
- **~1 frame latency** (16–33 ms) vs 500–1500 ms for RTB
- Used by Snipping Tool, Xbox Game Bar, OBS

**Plan:**

1. New engine: `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/WgcScreenshotCapture.cs` using `Windows.Graphics.Capture.GraphicsCaptureItem.CreateFromWindowId(hwnd)`
2. From the visual, walk to `HwndSource.FromVisual(...)` to get HWND
3. Capture 1 frame to `Direct3D11CaptureFramePool`, convert `IDirect3DSurface` → `WriteableBitmap` → PNG
4. For sub-element: compute bounds via `VisualTreeHelper.GetTransformToAncestor(hwndRoot)`, crop WGC frame
5. Drop `VisualCaptureUtil` / RTB path entirely — no fallback (if element is offscreen/hidden, return `ELEMENT_NOT_ONSCREEN` and require the agent to scroll/bring-into-view first; agents drive **visible** UI)

**Non-goals:**

- Capturing hidden/offscreen/minimized elements — agent UI automation always drives the visible window; force scroll-into-view as a prerequisite (cleaner semantics)
- Backwards compat with `VisualCaptureUtil` — delete it

## Acceptance criteria

- Full-window capture of MC main window succeeds **first try, <100ms**, returns a valid PNG that includes rendered D3D-interop content (MC video preview not black)
- Sub-element capture (button, title bar) <50ms
- No dispatcher starvation: 100 back-to-back captures all succeed
- `VisualCaptureUtil` + `ScreenshotCapture.cs` (RTB path) deleted
- Existing tests updated to assert captured pixel content, not just byte count
- Element-offscreen path returns `ELEMENT_NOT_ONSCREEN` with actionable suggestion (scroll container into view)

## Related

- DESKTOP-11470 (wpf-mcp side): Fast, reliable agentic UI automation for MotionCatalyst
- MC-1a Phase 3 findings: `/c/work/desktop/wpf-mcp/docs/brokered-mcp-validation-plan.md`

## M1-13: HMAC audit-log writer (Channel\<AuditEntry\>)

**PRD ref:** PRD §9.4 bug #10, FD-7, global rule S5.
**Depends on:** M1-01 (SessionPolicy provides session id).

  - Background `Task` reading a `Channel<AuditEntry>`.
  - Session key: `RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32)`.
  - `counterNonce`: `Interlocked.Increment`.
  - HMAC: `HMACSHA256` over `entryJson || prevHmac || sessionKey || counterNonce`.

avoids HMAC chain collision on `{sessionId}.jsonl` when broker and target
would otherwise race to write to the same file. The M2-21 acceptance test

title: FX-C6: FailureReason serializes as integer, not SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE string
description:
## Finding (Opus review: correctness)

**Files:** All `SnoopWPF.Agent.Tools/*Tool.cs` (27 files) — each has:

\`\`\`csharp
private static readonly JsonSerializerOptions SerializerOptions = new()
{
    PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase,
    WriteIndented = false,
};

{

    {
        PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase,
        WriteIndented = false,
        Converters = { new JsonStringEnumConverter(JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseUpper) },
    };
}
\`\`\`

(Use `.NET 8 JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseUpper` which emits SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE; net462 will need DataContractJsonSerializer workaround — see notes.)

2. Replace the 27 copies with `ToolSerializerOptions.Default`.
3. Update `SetPropertyToolTests.cs:80` + any other integer-form assertions to expect string form.

title: FX-M1: [ThreadStatic] pumpDepth breaks across thread-pool awaits
description:
## Finding

**File:** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/SnoopInspector.cs:52-54, :2850, :2862-2870`

`pumpDepth` is `[ThreadStatic]`. After `await PumpUntilIdleCoreAsync(...)` resumes on a different thread-pool thread, `pumpDepth--` decrements a different slot than `pumpDepth++` incremented. Counter diverges: incrementing thread keeps residual 1 forever → spurious DISPATCHER_BUSY; decrementing thread saw 0 → guard fails to prevent double-pump.

## Fix

Replace `[ThreadStatic] int pumpDepth` with instance-level `int _pumpInProgress`, guarded via `Interlocked.CompareExchange(ref _pumpInProgress, 1, 0)`. Return `DISPATCHER_BUSY` if already 1. Reset to 0 in `finally`.

## Acceptance

- Test: 2 concurrent `PumpUntilIdleAsync` calls → one wins, the other gets `DISPATCHER_BUSY`, no spurious failures on thread migration.
- Build + tests clean.

## Scope

- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/SnoopInspector.cs`
- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Tests/SnoopInspectorPumpGuardTests.cs` (new)

title: FX-C1: SnoopInspector.Dispose races with in-flight RunOnDispatcherAsync callers
description:
## Finding (Opus review: architecture/threading)

**File:** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/SnoopInspector.cs:122-133, :3239-3291`

`Dispose()` sets `disposed = true` then disposes `concurrencySemaphore`. A thread that already passed `ThrowIfDisposed()` at line 3223 but has not yet called `concurrencySemaphore.WaitAsync()` at line 3239 will hit `ObjectDisposedException` from the disposed semaphore instead of the clean one from `ThrowIfDisposed`.

## Fix

Acquire the semaphore under a pattern that checks `disposed` inside the finally, or use a CancellationTokenSource that is cancelled before the semaphore is disposed (so `WaitAsync` throws `OperationCanceledException` instead).

## Acceptance

- Race test: 1000 concurrent `RunOnDispatcherAsync` callers + disposal → no unhandled `ObjectDisposedException`.
- `dotnet.exe test SnoopWPF.Agent.Tests` clean.

## Scope (files)

- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/SnoopInspector.cs`
- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Tests/SnoopInspectorDisposeRaceTests.cs` (new)

title: M1-21: SnoopAgent.StartBrokered API
description:
## M1-21: `SnoopAgent.StartBrokered(app, pipeName, sessionTokenHex, opts)` API

> **NEW 2026-04-16** per architecture change. Read
> `ARCHITECTURE-CHANGE-2026-04-16-BROKERED-MODE.md` first.

**PRD ref:** PRD §4.1 Brokered mode, §4.2 brokered boot sequence, §9.7 Brokered pipe hardening.
**Depends on:** M1-01, M1-22.
**Estimated:** ~280 LOC + unit/integration tests.

**API signature**

```csharp
public static SnoopAgentHandle StartBrokered(
    Application app,
    string pipeName,
    string sessionTokenHex,
    SnoopAgentOptions opts);
```

**Required behaviour**

- Open `NamedPipeServerStream(pipeName, PipeDirection.InOut, maxAllowedInstances=1,
  PipeOptions.Asynchronous | PipeOptions.CurrentUserOnly)`.
- Perform the same `PerformPipeHandshakeAsync` pattern as
  `McpServerSetup.RunWithPipeAsync`: 5-second timeout,
  `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals` token compare,
  `sessionTokenHex` is the expected token.
- **Reconnect loop**: after the client disconnects, dispose the old
  `NamedPipeServerStream`, recreate it with the same options, then call
  `WaitForConnectionAsync` again. Loop indefinitely until `SnoopAgent.Stop()`
  is called or the process exits. This supports broker crash-and-restart
  without requiring a target restart.
- `Console.Out` is NOT touched — the target owns its own stdout; the broker
  (separate process) owns the MCP stdio anchor.

**Files to create/edit**

- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Server/SnoopAgent.cs` — add `StartBrokered(app, pipeName, sessionTokenHex, opts)`.
- `SnoopAgent.Stop()` (if not already present) — drains pending requests and
  closes the pipe gracefully so the broker sees a clean disconnect and the
  reconnect loop terminates.

**Tests**

- Unit test: mock-broker round-trip — broker client connects, sends a framed
  request, receives a framed response. Assert `Console.Out` is untouched
  (contrast with `StartCoLocated` which takes it over per M1-19).
- Reconnect test: broker disconnects mid-session, re-connects, next tool call
  succeeds (verifies the reconnect loop).
- Redaction target-side test: a `[Sensitive]`-marked DP's value arrives at the
  mock broker as the redaction sentinel, not the raw value.
- Negative test: client connecting without valid token → handshake rejection
  (constant-time compare, no timing leak).
- Negative test: connecting from a different Windows user account →
  `PipeOptions.CurrentUserOnly` refusal (pipe open fails at OS level).

**Acceptance criteria**

```bash
dotnet.exe test /c/work/snoopwpf/SnoopWPF.Agent.Tests \
    --filter "FullyQualifiedName~StartBrokered"
dotnet.exe test /c/work/snoopwpf/SnoopWPF.Agent.IntegrationTests \
    --filter "FullyQualifiedName~BrokeredRoundTrip"
```

**Commit**

```
feat(M1-21): SnoopAgent.StartBrokered — hardened named-pipe transport

PipeOptions.CurrentUserOnly + 256-bit token handshake (PerformPipeHandshakeAsync
pattern). Reconnect loop supports broker crash/restart. Console.Out untouched
(broker owns MCP stdio). Explicit sessionTokenHex parameter required.
```

title: FX-M7: Pipe name logged at Trace — remove disclosure
description:
## Finding

**File:** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Server/McpServerSetup.cs:335`

\`\`\`csharp
Trace.TraceInformation(
    \"SnoopWPF.Agent (Brokered) waiting for connection on pipe '{0}'.\", pipeName);
\`\`\`

On Windows, default TraceListener writes to OutputDebugString — readable by any process in the session via DebugView. Pipe name gives attackers the precise pipe address to race-connect.

## Fix

Remove pipe name from Trace output: \`Trace.TraceInformation(\"SnoopWPF.Agent (Brokered) waiting for connection.\")\`. If debugging is needed, emit at `Trace.WriteLineIf(conditional)` under a debug switch that is off by default.

## Acceptance

- Grep confirms no `Trace.*pipeName*` in production code.
- Build + tests clean.

## Scope

- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Server/McpServerSetup.cs`

title: FX-M3: Brokered pipe reconnect has no backoff — kernel pipe handle exhaustion risk
description:
## Finding

**File:** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Server/McpServerSetup.cs:322-390`

When `PerformPipeHandshakeAsync` fails (bad token, timeout, client disconnect during handshake), `continue` at line 355 immediately re-creates NamedPipeServerStream with no backoff. Hostile/misbehaving client can connect + fail handshake in a tight loop, exhausting kernel pipe handles (Windows caps at 254 named-pipe instances).

## Fix

After handshake failure, `await Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(250), ct)` before re-entering the accept loop. Optional: failure counter + exponential backoff up to 5 seconds.

## Acceptance

- Stress test: 500 bad-token connects in a tight loop → server stays responsive, no handle exhaustion.
- Build + tests clean.

## Scope

- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Server/McpServerSetup.cs`

title: FX-M2: CompositionRenderingResource.Dispose race with OnRendering
description:
## Finding

**File:** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/Sync/CompositionRenderingResource.cs:124-135`

`Dispose()` sets `disposed = true` on the calling thread, then posts `Unsubscribe` to the Dispatcher at `Send` priority. Between those events, the Dispatcher may fire `Rendering` → `OnRendering` aborts + re-assigns `idleProbe` after `Dispose()` already nulled/aborted it. Re-armed probe fires `OnContextIdle` → fires `IdleChanged` on potentially disposed registry → `ObjectDisposedException`.

## Fix

1. Add `if (this.disposed) return;` at top of `OnRendering` (symmetric with `OnContextIdle`).
2. Null `idleProbe` before posting `InvokeAsync(Unsubscribe)` in `Dispose`.

## Acceptance

- Stress test: rapid create/dispose cycle during active rendering → no exceptions.
- Build + tests clean.

## Scope

- `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/Sync/CompositionRenderingResource.cs`

description:
## M1-06: `ISnoopInspector` — WpfLocator overloads with NodeRegistry growth cap

**PRD ref:** PRD §6 bullet "Resolution cost bounds" (bug #9); PRD §14 bug #9.
**Depends on:** M1-05.
**Estimated:** ~250 LOC + tests; interface + resolver.

**Context.** Every ISnoopInspector method that takes `nodeId` gains a
`WpfLocator` overload. The resolver caps new `NodeRegistry` entries at 100
per resolution; overshoot returns `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`. Existing `nodeId`
overloads remain for compat (deprecated via analyzer in M1-17, not
`[Obsolete]`).

**Files to edit/create**

- **Edit** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Contracts/ISnoopInspector.cs`: add locator
  overloads for each existing nodeId method. Do not remove existing methods.
- **Create** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/LocatorResolver.cs`: resolves a
  `WpfLocator` against the current tree; tracks new-NodeRegistry-entry
  count per-call; throws `LocatorAmbiguousException` at cap.
- **Edit** `SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/SnoopInspector.cs`: implement the new
  interface overloads by delegating to `LocatorResolver` then calling the
  existing nodeId path.
- **Fix** `InspectElementDto.ParentNodeId` hardcoded empty string at
  `SnoopInspector.cs:462` (PRD §14 debt item). Parent resolution is now
  meaningful because locators can walk ancestors.
- **Edit** `SnoopWPF.Agent.IntegrationTests/TestWpfApp.cs` — add a
  `VirtualizingStackPanel`-backed `ListBox` named `testBigList` with
  `ItemsSource = Enumerable.Range(0, 10000).Select(i => $"Item {i}")` and
  `x:Name="testBigList"` (or the equivalent code-behind `Name` assignment).
  This fixture is required by the virtualized-list locator test below and
  by M2-04b.

**Tests**

- `SnoopWPF.Agent.IntegrationTests/LocatorResolutionTests.cs`:
  - Each of the four forms resolves on `TestWpfApp`.
  - Virtualized list with 10,000 items and a `viewModel=` locator: resolver
    returns `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` at the 100-entry cap (NOT OOM).
  - `path=` with two sibling buttons matches first (documented behaviour);
    analyzer SWPF0011 warns separately in M1-18.
  - `ParentNodeId` is non-empty for non-root elements.

**Acceptance criteria**

```bash
dotnet.exe test /c/work/snoopwpf/SnoopWPF.Agent.IntegrationTests \
    --filter "FullyQualifiedName~LocatorResolution"
# Cap is implemented
grep -q "100\|cap\|Cap" /c/work/snoopwpf/SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/LocatorResolver.cs
# ParentNodeId no longer hard-coded empty
! grep -q 'ParentNodeId.*string.Empty' /c/work/snoopwpf/SnoopWPF.Agent.Engine/SnoopInspector.cs
```

**Commit**
